question: Re-judgement of 26.09 (SCORECARD §0): criterion 8.2 Range 7.5 / 15, the largest gap: '1 STOP frame beyond 100 m on the organizers' objects; 0.3 m cubes at 43-53 m'. On set O (cloud_with_fake_obj, scored with scripts/score_fake_objects.py): big_center first STOP 98.0 m (held from 98.7), big_above first STOP 101.3 m but held only from 23.9 m (on wf14/integrate-p3; no hold on 00143b0), long_low_on_rails first STOP 82.2 m (held 90.8), small_center 52.5 m, small_on_rail 42.7 m, thin_hanging 30.1 m. What limits the first STOP / hold distance: physics (too few returns) or a config limit / rule (returns present but rejected)? Ship a range gain only through this pre-registration.

Real data: the same wrappers over the six recordings and the ride (new_data, 8 pieces as the gate) log every corridor blob with a strict-envelope voxel beyond 40 m and every `elevated` blob, plus per frame the returns within 0.9 m of the axis at 100-200 m just above the envelope top (3.0-3.6 m) and just below its floor (-0.5-0.12 m). Scripts: scratch (trace_setO.py, trace_pop.py), not committed.

false_alarm_cost_of_relaxing.reading: Relaxing the envelope beyond the bed range, or admitting flat or 3-4 voxel clusters as new tracks, would add candidates on about half of the ride's frames at 100-200 m: the far limits on set O objects are the height reference's, and they hold back real clutter. What is cheap is hysteresis on a track already confirmed: on the real data the shape signatures almost never hit a STOP track (1 logged cluster-frame on the ride beyond 40 m), while on set O they take the box at the envelope top down.

rules.tracking.stop_keep_signature: bool, false = off (today). true: a track reported as an obstacle (STOP, zone gauge) in the previous frame counts a hit whose cluster has >= gauge_min_points voxels inside the strict gauge but was demoted only by a shape signature (elevated, floating, edge, wall_face; clustering.SHAPE_SIGNATURES) as a hit inside the gauge in its zone vote. Never a column (the column hold), beyond_axis, beyond_height_ref, overhead or retro. It never makes a new obstacle: an unreported or advisory track votes as today. Reported reason 'stop_hold'. Geometry-general: a shape heuristic for infrastructure may keep a track from being confirmed; it does not take a confirmed obstacle down.
rules.tracking.stop_keep_thin: int, 0 = off (today). The corridor clusters flatter than cluster.min_height (one scan line), which are dropped today, are kept aside (Cluster.thin; no other stage sees them) and, after the association of the ordinary clusters, may continue a track that nothing matched, greedily with the same gate and prediction, when they are inside the gauge (zone gauge; or demoted by a shape signature for a STOP track with stop_keep_signature). 1: only a track reported as an obstacle in the previous frame (it cannot confirm anything new). 2: also a track not yet reported whose last hit was inside the gauge (the scan line counts towards its confirmation). A thin cluster never starts a track.

ship_rule.then: ship = the candidate's values become the defaults in configs/default.yaml (and the ROS parameter file via scripts/sync_params.sh); otherwise the flags stay off and the candidates are recorded as tried, not shipped
ship_rule.priority: safety wins over false-alarm gains; a range gain must not add false STOPs on the ride

rule.tracking.stop_keep_min_voxels: int, 0 = no bar (round 1's rules). > 0: a cluster counts for a STOP track through stop_keep_signature or stop_keep_thin only when it has at least this many voxels inside the strict envelope (Cluster.n_gauge). cap.rule: the keep rules act on a track only while its last clean hit (an obstacle cluster inside the envelope, zone gauge, not a scan line) is at most 10 s of sensor time ago, summed from the measured frame intervals (the nominal period without one): the same at 10 and 5 Hz (the rate-independence rule of 25.09); past it the track falls back to the behaviour without the keep rules; a clean hit resets it; a track never seen clean is never kept
